correctness.rationale: Claim precisely concerns two-sided Fibonacci-language shift with allowed (n+1)-blocks, log base e, m>=3 and F_m-1<=n<=F_(m+1)-2. The length-n Rauzy edge graph presents that SFT. At every nonbispecial n, unique-sided extension prevents missing concatenations, making G_(n+1) its directed line graph: the nonzero spectrum of incidence RS/SR is identical. Published Fibonacci Sturmian bispecial classification gives n=F_(m+1)-2 exactly two first-return circuits of lengths F_(m−1),F_m, so the strictly decreasing return series z^a+z^b hits 1 at unique z in (0,1), proving e^(−a h)+e^(−b h)=1; adjacent bispecial endpoints and line-graph propagation give every index and n=1 boundary. Defining c_m=F_m h, the adjacent Fibonacci ratio tends to 1/phi, whence c_m -> unique positive c with e^(−c/phi)+e^(−c)=1. The full interval of achievable n/F_m mesh limits [1,phi] gives all cluster points [c,phi c], and h=O(1/n). Independently constructed finite Fibonacci factor graphs for n=1..200 matched counts n+1/n+2, single branch and predicted two first-return lengths, and direct numpy adjacency eigenanalysis for n=1..32 satisfied the claimed root equation with maximum residual 2.09e−14. Numerical 0.87391396549 and 1.41402249941 independently recovered. These bounded checks corroborate, never replace the structural infinite proof.
